item.title: Republican 'Muslim Brotherhood' attacks on El-Sayed in Michigan seek to exploit Democratic fault lines
item.description: In Michigan, Republican US Senate candidate Mike Rogers and allies are escalating their efforts to tie Democratic rival Abdul El-Sayed to the Muslim Brotherhood, with President Donald Trump falsely branding him a "jihadist."
item.dc:creator: David Morgan
item.content:encoded: Republican US Senate candidate Mike Rogers and allies including President Donald Trump are escalating their efforts to tie Democratic rival Abdul El-Sayed to the Muslim Brotherhood less than two weeks before the [USN:L1N4600TJ TEXT:"November 3 midterms"], with Trump falsely branding him a "jihadist." Pollsters and political strategists say the approach is aimed at dissuading Jewish and Black voters in the Detroit area who backed El-Sayed's primary opponent, Haley Stevens, from getting behind the Democratic nominee in the closing days of the Senate campaign in Michigan. "It gives them even more reason to pause and not vote for El-Sayed," said Dennis Darnoi, a Republican political consultant. "If Democratic voters aren't casting ballots for El-Sayed in what is the biggest population area here, then that is a net benefit to Mike Rogers' campaign." El-Sayed and Rogers are vying for the seat held by retiring Democratic Senator Gary Peters in a race that could determine whether Democrats gain the four Senate seats needed to take control of the chamber in next month's election. Republicans currently have a 53-47 seat majority, which would be harder to overturn if El-Sayed loses. The Democrat has built a small lead in opinion polls by focusing his campaign on affordability, healthcare and getting money out of politics. Rogers has sought to undermine the Democrat's support among Jewish voters by pointing to El-Sayed's criticism of Israel's offensive in Gaza and asserting that El-Sayed has longstanding family ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, one of the Arab world's oldest and most influential Islamist groups. Strategists said homing in on the Muslim Brotherhood also aims to hurt El-Sayed by exploiting economic tensions between Black voters and Michigan's large Arab-American community. Rogers has pointed to old social media posts by El-Sayed's half sister saying their mother was involved with the organization in the 1970s. El-Sayed has disavowed the Muslim Brotherhood, denied any connection with the group and has said that he was not raised by his mother. His parents divorced when he was 3 years old, and he was raised by his father and step-mother. Asked about Rogers' strategy, campaign spokesperson Alyssa Brouillet said El-Sayed's "extremist positions" on issues ranging from prisons to the Muslim Brotherhood were alienating Michiganders. El-Sayed campaign spokesperson Roxie Richner said Rogers is trying to distract from the economic effects of Trump's agenda, adding in a statement: "Independent fact checkers have repeatedly debunked Mike’s lies, but their campaign continues to use bad faith attacks on Abdul's faith and family." 'PROUD TO BE AN AMERICAN' Rogers hit the Muslim Brotherhood message hard during this week's televised debate, questioning the Democrat's loyalty to the US. "If you are going to go to the United States Senate, we need to know: are you for America or are you for these terrorist groups overseas?" Rogers asked. El-Sayed, a son of Egyptian immigrants who would be the first Muslim to be elected to the US Senate if he wins, responded by calling the question shameful. "It's actually quite beneath you, Mike," he replied. "I am proud of America. I'm proud to be an American. I'm proud of our Constitution that guarantees all of us the right to pray as we choose to pray." Rogers, a former congressman, US Army officer and FBI agent, later appealed directly to Democrats who voted for Stevens, saying they "have a home" with him if they were worried that El-Sayed was too "extreme." MICHIGAN SENATE RACE A 'TOSS-UP' It is unclear if the Republican strategy is paying off. The race is rated a toss-up by independent political analysts, with polls showing El-Sayed with an average lead of 2.6 percentage points, according to the website RealClearPolling.com. El-Sayed has campaigned recently with prominent Black political figures such as Senator Raphael Warnock of Georgia, Representative Ayanna Pressley of Massachusetts and 2024 Democratic presidential candidate Kamala Harris. Former President Barack Obama, who has endorsed El-Sayed, is due to campaign with him on Saturday. Michigan Democratic Party Black Caucus Chair Keith Williams, who backed Stevens in Michigan's Democratic primary contest and is now working to rally support for El-Sayed, acknowledged that tensions between the Black and Arab American communities are an issue for the candidate. "We have to work through our differences," Williams told Reuters. "At the end of the day, this election is bigger than our differences because we cannot have a senator going to Washington and supporting Donald Trump's policies." Some strategists say the attacks may have come too late to reshape the race and risk backfiring if voters view them as anti-Muslim. "I don't know what this does for them," said Jim Zogby, a longtime pollster and co-founder of the Arab American Institute, a nonprofit that advocates for the Arab American community. "There are people who think Haitians eat cats and dogs and think anybody with an Arabic name is either a terrorist or a member of the Muslim Brotherhood. But that's a much smaller group of people - and it's already a Republican group of people." OVERWHELMING SUPPORT FROM BLACK VOTERS A September Emerson College poll showed support for El-Sayed at 81% among Black voters, who make up about a quarter of Michigan Democrats. "There was no sign there in mid-September of erosion of Black support for El-Sayed. I would not suspect that the number would have changed much over the last month," said Matt Taglia, senior director of Emerson College Polling. Democrat Jocelyn Benson, who is running for Michigan governor, scored 4 percentage points higher in the same poll, while Harris drew 86% of the Black vote in 2024. Michigan pollster Steve Mitchell said weaker support among Black and Jewish voters could cost El-Sayed as many as 20,000 votes. Rogers lost his 2024 Senate bid to Democrat Elissa Slotkin by a similar margin.

item.title: Gunman fires from car near Paris, killing 1; police arrest suspect
item.description: The shooting comes at a moment of particular tension in France, after nationwide protests turned violent last Saturday and ahead of possible unrest this coming weekend.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A gunman opened fire from a car outside Paris, killing one person and wounding four others including a 12-year-old girl on Friday, French authorities said. "We would like to thank our law enforcement agencies, which have already taken the suspect into custody. The National Anti-Terrorism Prosecutor's Office has taken over the case," President Emmanuel Macron said in a post on X, expressing deep sorrow over the killing. The shooting comes at a moment of particular tension in France, after nationwide protests [USN:L1N46908B TEXT:"turned violent"] last Saturday and ahead of possible unrest this coming weekend. Ali Rabeh, the mayor of the town of Trappes west of Paris, told BFMTV that a man had fired shoots from his car and "appeared to be firing at random and seemed intent on carrying out a massacre". Rabeh said the gunman was driving on a road from Trappes to neighbouring La Verriere and lived in a nearby town. Broadcaster BFM reported that the wounded 12-year-old girl had been hit eight times. The anti-terrorism prosecutor's office said its investigation included looking at whether the shooting was a terrorist act or if it were racially or religiously motivated.

item.title: Volkswagen-Les salariés menacent de faire grève si les accords ne sont pas respectés
item.description: Les dirigeants syndicaux allemands ont menacé d'organiser des grèves chez Volkswagen à partir de janvier, si l'entreprise ne revient pas d'ici fin octobre sur sa récente annulation des accords salariaux, marquant ainsi une escalade des conflits sociaux au sein du groupe.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les dirigeants syndicaux allemands ont menacé d'organiser des grèves chez Volkswagen (VOWG.DE) à partir de janvier, si l'entreprise ne revient pas d'ici fin octobre sur sa récente annulation des accords salariaux, marquant ainsi une escalade des conflits sociaux au sein du groupe. "Nous donnons à l'entreprise jusqu'à la fin du mois d'octobre pour retirer cet avis de résiliation", a déclaré Thorsten Groeger, du syndicat IG Metall, lors d'une conférence de presse. "Sinon, un processus de grande ampleur sera enclenché qui, je tiens à le préciser, ouvrira la voie à des actions collectives chez Volkswagen", a-t-il ajouté, suggérant des grèves. Une trêve excluant toute grève au sein de l’entreprise expire le 1er janvier 2027. Le premier constructeur automobile européen prévoit de [USN:L6N43F0NW TEXT:"supprimer"] 100.000 emplois et pourrait fermer jusqu’à quatre usines en Allemagne, alors qu’il est confronté à une concurrence chinoise de plus en plus intense, à des milliards de coûts liés aux droits de douane et à une transition coûteuse vers les véhicules électriques. Le conflit avec les délégués du personnel au sujet des réductions prévues a atteint son paroxysme le mois dernier, lorsque Volkswagen a résilié la quasi-totalité des accords salariaux conclus avec ses salariés allemands, remettant ainsi sur la table des négociations des normes de travail établies de longue date, notamment en matière de temps de travail et d’indemnités de congés payés. Le syndicat accuse le constructeur de se soustraire aux engagements pris dans le cadre d’un accord historique conclu fin 2024, tandis que Volkswagen affirme explorer toutes les options possibles pour réduire les coûts et préserver sa compétitivité. Le comité d'entreprise a déclaré lundi que son directoire prévoyait de geler les salaires de 660.000 salariés à travers le monde jusqu'en 2030. "Nous savons quelles conditions d'exploitation ont changé, mais nous savons aussi lesquelles étaient prévisibles, et nous attendons du directoire le mieux rémunéré de ce pays qu'il travaille avec nous pour trouver une solution", a commenté la présidente du comité d'entreprise, Daniela Cavallo. Le groupe a refusé de s'exprimer sur les mesures spécifiques de réduction des coûts et de restructuration qu'elle pourrait mettre en œuvre dans le cadre des négociations salariales allemandes, qui doivent débuter au plus tard début décembre, Thorsten Groeger ayant appelé à ce qu'elles commencent dès le 24 novembre. Une option pourrait être la création d'une "société de transfert", mise en place avec le soutien de l'Agence fédérale pour l'emploi afin de reconvertir les salariés et de les aider à trouver un nouvel emploi en dehors de Volkswagen.

item.title: India plans jobs survey changes to add unpaid work, improve gig worker data
item.description: India has proposed changes to its employment survey to better capture digital platform gig and unpaid work, the statistics ministry said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Shubham Batra, Manoj Kumar
item.content:encoded: India has proposed changes to its employment survey to better capture digital platform gig and unpaid work, the statistics ministry said on Friday. The revisions come amid a [USN:L1N3TJ071 TEXT:"debate"] over whether the official jobs data reflects underemployment and the quality of jobs in the world's most populous country, where the headline unemployment (INUNR=ECI) stands at 5%. While changes to the Periodic Labour Force Survey will affect comparisons with past data, India is aiming to tweak how it defines and measures employment while expanding the ambit of the survey. The survey will add a separate category for digital platform workers as the existing method did not capture enough of them, the ministry said. As part of this, it will ask a wider set of respondents across rural and urban households if members are engaged in digital platform work. India has seen a 55% increase in gig workers in the five years to 2025-26, the government's economic survey said in January, estimating that such workers may make up 2% of the total workforce in the country. MEASURING UNPAID WORK The changes proposed to the jobs survey will also measure activities that are usually not paid for, including production of goods for own use, household and caregiving activities, volunteer and unpaid trainee work. "This initiative to estimate platform gig workers is a half-step as there are a large number of informal gig workers who are not on any platform," said K.R. Shyam Sundar, a labour economist and a former professor at XLRI Jamshedpur. "However, capturing unpaid work in the PLFS survey is an important step ... and could eventually lead to changes in the methodology used to calculate national income as well." The changes will kick in from January 2027, with fresh samples for 2027-28. The government has invited public and expert feedback on the proposals within 15 days.

item.title: Weight-loss drugs fuel protein boom, but with more consumer scrutiny
item.description: Even as consumers seek out new sources of protein for their diets, they are becoming more skeptical of foods advertised as high-protein.
item.dc:creator: Waylon Cunningham, Nicholas Brown
item.content:encoded: Protein-infused bottled water. Ice cream. Boxed macaroni and cheese. Even vodka. The rise of weight-loss drugs is driving a boom in protein-based products, as users of GLP-1 medication like Novo Nordisk's (NOVOb.CO) Ozempic and Eli Lilly's (LLY.N) Mounjaro look for ways to counter the muscle loss those drugs can cause. GLP-1 users say they will spend 11% more on high-protein foods than before starting the drugs, according to an August survey from Boston Consulting Group. This is the fifth story in a five-part Reuters series on how weight-loss drugs are changing the way people shop and eat, and how companies are responding to the trend. Even as consumers seek out new sources of protein for their diets, they are becoming more skeptical of foods advertised as high-protein, Reuters interviews with consumers and company executives found. Some shoppers question whether products contain as much protein as advertising implies, while blanching at those that pack in so many additives or sugar that they undercut the health pitch. A report from marketing research firm NielsenIQ earlier this year said the snack industry has entered its "accountability era," noting that 25% of its survey respondents this year said they are using scanning apps to check the nutritional value of products, up from around 17% last year. "Protein is no longer a differentiator," said Chris Costagli, a lead marketing researcher at NielsenIQ, who co-wrote the report. Megan Gisela Bautista, a nonprofit employee in Maryland who does strength training, was recently disappointed by the protein content of a chicken jerky snack that touted high protein in a large, colorful font. "I'd have to eat five of them," Bautista said. "That's bad for you." Zack Spears of Dallas said he is checking nutritional labels regularly, and now watches YouTube videos from an online content creator who reviews protein-marketed products. "As this protein craze pops off, and things are getting more expensive, I want to be sure what I'm putting in my body is healthy," Spears said. Some brands acknowledge the growing consumer scrutiny. “Protein is here to stay, but the conversation must evolve,” said Susan Zaripheh, North America chief research officer for yogurt maker Danone (DANO.PA) , in a statement to Reuters. “Consumers are starting to look ‘beyond the gram,’ becoming more informed in the nuances of protein source and nutrient density.” Over the summer, the French food company filed a false advertising [USN:L6N42P17H TEXT:"lawsuit"] against rival yogurt maker Chobani, accusing it of inflating its protein claims on labels by using non-standard serving sizes. Chobani has disputed those claims, telling Reuters in a statement that its labeling is accurate and transparent. Zaripheh said consumers want products that also aid in digestibility and contain other nutrients like fiber. In addition to existing high-protein yogurts and soy milks, the company is developing products that combine protein with other nutrients. Globe Market Research estimated over the summer that the worldwide protein-enriched food market was worth nearly $58 billion last year. But Hormel Foods (HRL.N) , well-known for protein-heavy products like Spam and canned lunch meats, said it is avoiding the use of additives to increase protein in its products. "We believe that in the long run, people don't want too much science in their food," said Jason Levine, Hormel chief marketing officer, referring to additives like "whey powder or pea powder or scientifically engineered protein isolates." SCRUTINIZING LABELS Reuters found several brands that advertise protein content based on a larger portion size than used in regular versions of the same product, including in pastas, oatmeals and granolas. Nature Valley, a snack brand owned by General Mills (GIS.N) , sells a version of its “oats ‘n honey” loose granola that advertises 13 grams of protein on its packaging, based on a 2/3 cup (65 grams) serving size, more than twice as big as the 1/4 cup (27 grams) it calls a serving size for its regular, non-enhanced granola. General Mills, in a statement, said it considers the regular version a snack while the protein version can be eaten either as a snack or a more complete cereal meal. The product's protein-to-calorie ratio, a metric dietitians use to describe a product's protein content, indicates a “very low amount of protein overall,” said Jonathan Bonnet, a Stanford professor and chief medical officer at the Ardmore Institute of Health, adding that a glass of skim milk has more protein than the 2/3-cup serving. Bonnet said more patients are asking him lately for guidance on their protein intake. Still, other companies are expanding their offerings to meet demand. Researcher Circana reported in August that around 48% of US adults are looking to add protein in their diets, up 7 points from last year. Discount supermarket chain Aldi recently told Reuters it is launching a new line of private-label protein pancakes in October, the latest in a string of high-protein items released this year that have included sparkling water, crackers and wagyu beef jerky. Walmart will start selling a new, protein-infused instant coffee product from J.M. Smucker's (SJM.N) Folgers from November until January exclusively, Walmart told Reuters last month. Some consumers and dietitians say the protein trend has led people to eat more protein than they need. NielsenIQ's report said a third of more than 1,000 surveyed respondents believe the food industry is overhyping protein — and another third believe some products have too much protein. Dana Hunnes, a professor and clinical dietitian at UCLA, says the average person doesn't need as much protein as industry marketing has promoted. And some protein-marketed products have too many processed ingredients to qualify as healthy, Hunnes said. “I’ve seen the equivalent of a candy bar” advertising protein, she said. “Just because it has protein doesn’t mean it’s something you should eat." item.content:encoded: Ein mit 40.000 Tonnen russischem Diesel beladener Tanker ist auf dem Weg nach New York. Dies ging am Freitag aus einer Reuters-Auswertung von Schifffahrtsdaten des Finanzdienstleisters LSEG hervor. Es handelt sich um die erste Lieferung dieser Art seit dem von der damaligen Regierung unter Präsident Joe Biden 2022 wegen des Ukraine-Kriegs verhängten Importverbot für russisches Öl und Ölprodukte. Sie ist Teil einer Vereinbarung zwischen US-Präsident Donald Trump und dem russischen Präsidenten Wladimir Putin. Trump hofft, mit mehreren Maßnahmen die Dieselpreise vor den US-Zwischenwahlen am 3. November zu senken. Dazu gehört auch die Aussetzung von Teilen eines neuen Sanktionsgesetzes gegen Russland. Der unter maltesischer Flagge fahrende Tanker "Agioi Fanendes" wurde den Schifffahrtsdaten zufolge am 22. Oktober im russischen Ostseehafen Primorsk mit schwefelarmem Diesel beladen. Er soll am 7. November in den USA eintreffen. Wer Käufer und Verkäufer der Ladung sind, war zunächst nicht bekannt. Ein Kreml-Sprecher bestätigte am Freitag, dass ein erstes Schiff im Rahmen der Vereinbarung ausgelaufen sei. Er ließ jedoch offen, ob es für den US-Markt oder einen anderen bestimmt ist. "Soweit ich weiß, gab es bereits Berichte aus dem Energieministerium, dass der erste Tanker tatsächlich zu seinen Empfängern, seinen Käufern, ausgelaufen ist", sagte Dmitri Peskow. "Weitere Lieferungen werden von nun an in gleichmäßigem Tempo fortgesetzt." Russland hatte zugestimmt, ein selbst auferlegtes Exportverbot für Diesel aufzuheben, um den Kraftstoff wieder auf die Weltmärkte zu liefern. Trump hatte am 9. Oktober angekündigt, dass Russland zunächst 300.000 Tonnen oder 2,25 Millionen Barrel exportieren werde. Darauf sollen 500.000 Tonnen im November und eine Million Tonnen "unmittelbar danach" folgen. Der stellvertretende russische Ministerpräsident Alexander Nowak erklärte vergangene Woche, Russland könne seine Dieselausfuhren bis zum Jahresende auf das übliche Volumen von drei bis 3,5 Millionen Tonnen pro Monat steigern. Seit dem Inkrafttreten des vollständigen EU-Embargos gegen russische Ölprodukte im Februar 2023 wegen des Krieges in der Ukraine hat Russland Diesel hauptsächlich nach Brasilien, in die Türkei sowie in afrikanische Länder exportiert. Auch nach der Aufhebung des jüngsten, selbst auferlegten Exportverbots wegen Knappheiten infolge ukrainischer Angriffe wurden den Schifffahrtsdaten zufolge wieder Ladungen für die traditionellen Bestimmungsorte wie die Türkei und Brasilien verladen. Bei anderen Tankern, die in Primorsk beladen wurden, war das Ziel zunächst unklar.

item.title: Failte-Sigenergy JV to build inverter, battery storage plants in India
item.description: A joint venture between India's Failte Energy and China-based Sigenergy plans to invest an initial $250 million in India to set up manufacturing facilities for inverters and battery energy storage systems, a senior company executive said.
item.dc:creator: Sethuraman R
item.content:encoded: A joint venture between India's Failte Energy and China-based Sigenergy plans to invest an initial $250 million in India to set up manufacturing facilities for inverters and battery energy storage systems, a senior company executive said. The company, which began operations in India earlier this year, will first build an inverter manufacturing plant that is expected to be operational by the second quarter of 2027, Rahul Morde, head of sales for Sigenergy-India, told Reuters Failte-Sigenergy is exploring possible locations for the factory The company will subsequently establish a battery energy storage systems factory, which is expected to come online six to eight months after the inverter facility, Morde said on the sidelines of Renewable Energy India Expo The company also plans to set up a research and development centre focused on battery energy storage systems in India, he said Sigenergy has complied with India's regulations on storing data in the country and is seeking investment clearances, Morde said India is looking to rapidly expand renewable energy capacity and grid-scale energy storage to support its clean energy goals, creating opportunities for manufacturers Sigenergy develops and manufactures energy storage systems, including battery products, inverters and energy management software for residential and commercial customers The company [USN:L1N40Z012 TEXT:"debuted"] on the Hong Kong stock market in April after raising HK$4.4 billion ($562 million) through an initial public offering (This story has been corrected to clarify that the joint venture, not China's Sigenergy, will invest in India, in the headline and paragraph 1.)

item.title: Austria expels four Russian diplomats on security grounds
item.description: Austria's foreign ministry said on Friday it was expelling four Vienna-based Russian diplomats over "activities incompatible with their diplomatic status", a term usually used for spying.
item.dc:creator: Francois Murphy
item.content:encoded: Austria's foreign ministry said on Friday it was expelling four Vienna-based Russian diplomats over "activities incompatible with their diplomatic status", a term usually used for spying. "Based on findings by the Austrian security authorities, the Austrian foreign ministry has taken measures against four Russian diplomats in Vienna," it said in a statement, adding that they had been declared personae non gratae and ordered to leave the country. Three of them worked at Russia's embassy to Austria and one at the Russian delegation to the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) on military security and arms control, the ministry said. The move brings to 18 the number of Russian diplomats Austria has expelled since 2020. While Austria is a neutral country, politically its governments have sided with Ukraine since Russia launched its all-out invasion in 2022. "Vienna is thoughtlessly following the West's anti-Russian policy, and there will inevitably be an appropriate response to such measures," the Russian embassy said in a statement on its website, describing the expulsions as "a further unfriendly step" towards Russia by the Austrian authorities. While Austria does not usually comment on the specifics of such expulsions, during the [USN:L1N41H088 TEXT:"last round"] in May, when it expelled three Russian diplomats, it said it was because of an "antenna forest" on the roofs of Russian diplomatic buildings that could be used for spying. Vienna is a major diplomatic centre, hosting the OSCE and United Nations organisations such as the International Atomic Energy Agency. Larger countries like Russia and the United States often have separate ambassadors to Austria, the OSCE and UN organisations, each running an embassy or mission. Vienna, which was divided into Allied sectors after World War Two, has long had a reputation as a den of spies. The large diplomatic presence offers the opportunity to station intelligence agents there under cover of diplomatic immunity.

item.title: Wizz Air offers UK pilots voluntary redundancy, union says
item.description: Wizz Air has offered voluntary redundancy to some pilots at London's Luton airport, its primary UK base, an association representing British pilots said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Wizz Air (WIZZ.L) has offered voluntary redundancy to some pilots at London's Luton airport, its primary UK base, an association representing British pilots said on Friday. Hungarian budget carrier Wizz [USN:L6N4590BY TEXT:"cut"] its winter capacity by 5% last month in a bid to offset high jet fuel prices triggered by the Iran war, even as its hedging policy and liquidity place it among the better positioned airlines. "BALPA is supporting and advising its members on the offer that has been made", the British Airline Pilots' Association said in an e-mailed statement, confirming a Bloomberg News report that Wizz had offered expressions of interest for first officers at Luton to leave on voluntary enhanced terms. BALPA said its UK pilots would "welcome constructive dialogue" with Wizz, which at its most recent capital markets day event said it employs a total of 2,650 pilots. Wizz did not respond to a request for comment on BALPA's statement. Latvian carrier [USN:L6N4560BF TEXT:"airBaltic"] filed for bankruptcy in September, in a sign that smaller airlines were at risk of collapse from a sector-wide crisis resulting from the Iran conflict.

item.title: France mounts major security operation for fresh wave of protests
item.description: France will deploy 70,000 police backed by specialist units for protests on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said, accusing ultra-left groups of encouraging violence and looting after unrest shocked the country last weekend.
item.dc:creator: Makini Brice, Dominique Vidalon
item.content:encoded: France will deploy 70,000 police backed by specialist units for protests on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Friday, accusing ultra-left groups of encouraging violence and looting after unrest [USN:L1N46608H TEXT:"shocked the country"] last weekend. The government is seeking to prevent a repeat of last week's demonstrations that descended into riots, looting and arson in several cities, triggering widespread criticism of authorities for not preventing the mayhem. "We will be uncompromising with rioters, looters and all those who commit acts of violence," Nunez told reporters on Friday after meetings involving President Emmanuel Macron, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu and senior security officials. Nunez said authorities had identified numerous online calls from hard-left groups encouraging attacks and urging activists to target public buildings. "We are not talking about a nice, friendly demonstration," Nunez said, adding: "We are ready for tomorrow. We will be extremely vigilant, extremely firm, and we will let absolutely nothing pass." MUSEUMS, MAJOR EVENTS SHUTTERED AS PRECAUTION Anger over living costs and strained public services has drawn students, workers and unions onto the streets of France in recent weeks, but authorities say radical militants and bands of young looters have taken advantage of the dispute to sow chaos. Police have authorised only a union demonstration in Paris on Saturday, rejecting requests for rallies lodged by France's main student union, UNEF, and the Yellow Vest movement, an anti-establishment force that first emerged in 2018. Many French cities beyond Paris have also banned protests, including France's second and third largest cities, Marseille and Lyon. UNEF said its rallies, which grew from high school protests last month against teacher shortages and shabby facilities, would go ahead regardless. Fears of renewed turmoil prompted several of Paris' best-known cultural institutions, including the Louvre, to close on Saturday, while the city's normally bustling Art Basel fair will remain shut throughout the weekend. Business groups also urged shops to stay shut after some 3,000 stores and businesses were ransacked last weekend. Nunez said 10,000 more police would be on the streets than a week ago, while the specialist RAID and GIGN units, mounted police, helicopters, drones and anti-drone systems would be deployed across the country. Armoured vehicles and water cannon vehicles would also be available, while curfews imposed in some sensitive areas this past week would remain in force. FAR-RIGHT CONGRESS A POSSIBLE FLASHPOINT Authorities are also concerned that the annual congress of Marine Le Pen's far-right National Rally in Orleans this weekend could become a flashpoint, with left-wing and anti-racist groups announcing counter-demonstrations. The upsurge of violence has boosted poll ratings for Le Pen, who is the frontrunner for next year's presidential election. She has portrayed the unrest as evidence of a collapse in state authority. Adding to tensions, one person was killed and four [USN:L6N4690NC TEXT:"injured"] in a shooting west of Paris on Friday in an attack that police said could be racially motivated. Macron is due to meet student representatives later on Friday for the first time, seeking to de-escalate a crisis that has exposed deep social and political tensions. Marylise Leon, the general secretary of the CFDT, one of the nation's largest trade unions, criticised him on Friday for refusing to grant permission to more rallies on Saturday. "It's counterproductive because there is a lot of anger, a lot of anger and a demand to be considered and to be listened to," she told French broadcaster TF1. "It's not for the president to decide who can legitimately request to protest." The social turbulence has intensified scrutiny of France's economic outlook and ratings agency Moody's is widely expected to cut the [USN:L8N4682H3 TEXT:"French credit rating"] on Friday, underscoring concern that the government had not reined in public spending.

item.title: BOURSE Kering dévisse après un recul des ventes de Gucci, rude hiver en vue pour le luxe (actualisé)
item.description: L'action Kering dévisse de 12% vendredi, au lendemain des résultats trimestriels du géant français du luxe, marqués par un nouveau recul des ventes de Gucci, sa marque phare, le groupe maintenant néanmoins le cap sur le plan de redressement engagé par son directeur général, Luca de Meo.
item.dc:creator: Helen Reid, Elena Smirnova
item.content:encoded: L'action Kering (PRTP.PA) dévisse de 12% vendredi, au lendemain des résultats trimestriels du géant français du luxe, marqués par un nouveau recul des ventes de Gucci, sa marque phare, le groupe maintenant néanmoins le cap sur le plan de redressement engagé par son directeur général, Luca de Meo. À la Bourse de Paris, vers 10h55 GMT, l'action chutait de 12,67% à 186,4 euros, lanterne rouge d'un CAC 40 (.FCHI) en repli de 0,71% au même moment. Les ventes de Gucci, qui représentent environ la moitié du résultat opérationnel, se sont établies à 1,29 milliard d'euros au cours du trimestre, [USN:L8N46828Z TEXT:"a déclaré Kering mercredi"]. Sur l'ensemble du groupe, le chiffre d'affaires a reculé de 1% à données comparables. "Nous relevons que les perspectives de Kering ne font plus mention d'une ambition de retour à la croissance (en 2026, présumons-nous)", remarquent les analystes de Bernstein. La reprise longtemps promise par les groupes du luxe semble plus que jamais hors de portée. L'extension du conflit au Moyen-Orient, conjuguée au renforcement de la pression fiscale sur les plus fortunés en Chine, a accentué les difficultés des plus grands acteurs mondiaux du secteur au troisième trimestre, les dirigeants se préparant à un hiver difficile. Les récentes [USN:L8N4650AN TEXT:"émeutes à Paris"], qui ont laissé des vitrines de boutiques Louis Vuitton brisées et vu des vélos électriques incendiés près de la place Vendôme, haut lieu du shopping de luxe, ont mis en lumière les risques politiques auxquels les marques de prestige sont confrontées non seulement à l'étranger, mais aussi dans leur propre pays. Les titres [USN:L8N4680BW TEXT:"LVMH"] (LVMH.PA) et [USN:L8N4680BW TEXT:"Hermès"] (HRMS.PA) reculaient également de 1% à 1,5% vendredi, alors que les cours du pétrole brut touchaient leur plus haut niveau depuis le début du mois de mai, accentuant la pression sur le pouvoir d'achat des ménages et limitant leur capacité à dépenser dans les sacs à main et les vêtements coûteux. Harsharan Mann, gérante de portefeuille actions mondiales chez Aviva Investors, basé à Londres, souligne que les marques de luxe pourraient devoir réduire davantage les prix de leurs produits d'entrée de gamme afin d'attirer de nouveau les consommateurs. "Si les prix restent encore un peu déconnectés de la réalité ou si les consommateurs continuent de penser qu'ils sont trop élevés pour être acceptables, alors vous pouvez avoir la meilleure créativité du monde, mais les consommateurs vont-ils réellement adhérer au produit ?", a-t-elle déclaré. GUCCI PEINE À SE REDRESSER Le recul de Gucci s'est poursuivi malgré le plan de Luca de Meo visant à rendre les produits de la marque plus attractifs pour les consommateurs de la classe moyenne et l'arrivée en magasin, à la mi-juillet, de la collection Primavera conçue par son nouveau directeur artistique Demna, qui comprend notamment une robe moulante ornée de cristaux vendue 5.900 dollars (5.269,74 euros). Malgré une amélioration dans le canal de gros, les ventes globales de Gucci ont reculé de 6%. "Compte tenu du recul de 6% de Gucci et du ralentissement de la demande, un retour à la croissance au quatrième trimestre paraît peu probable", estiment les analystes de TD Cowen. Selon les analystes de JP Morgan, les performances de Gucci ont été affectées par le contexte général, un nombre réduit de lancements de nouveaux produits au cours du trimestre, ainsi que par des comparaisons plus difficiles. "Compte tenu du recul enregistré par Gucci au cours du trimestre, rien n'indique pour l'instant que l'accélération du renouvellement de la gamme soit en train de marquer un tournant", affirme le courtier dans une note. La directrice financière de Kering a indiqué que le redressement de la marque serait "graduel" et que la faiblesse de la fréquentation des magasins constituait le principal défi, en particulier en Chine. TD Cowen souligne que "la baisse séquentielle a été principalement provoquée par la poursuite du recul de la fréquentation des magasins", même si "le taux de conversion, le prix moyen ainsi que le panier moyen ont continué de progresser à mesure que les nouvelles collections étaient déployées". LE TITRE PERD DE L'ÉLAN UN AN APRÈS L'ARRIVÉE DE LUCA DE MEO Alors que Kering peine à mener à bien le redressement de Gucci dans un contexte économique peu porteur, même Hermès, positionné sur le très haut de gamme, montre des signes de ralentissement. Les ventes de sa division Vêtement et Accessoires ont reculé de 2% au troisième trimestre, pénalisées par la faiblesse de la demande en Chine. Au total, le groupe a enregistré sa plus faible croissance trimestrielle des ventes depuis 2020. Dans l'ensemble du secteur, les valorisations ont été durement affectées, les investisseurs réévaluant les perspectives de croissance. L'action Hermès a ainsi perdu 40% de sa valeur depuis le 1er janvier, à son plus bas niveau depuis 2014, tandis que celle de LVMH est tombée à un plus bas de dix ans. Chez Kering, toutefois, les interrogations portent avant tout sur la capacité de Gucci à renouer avec la croissance.

item.title: Kenya Red Cross rushes aid to Ethiopians who crossed border fleeing violence
item.description: The Kenya Red Cross said it was sending humanitarian supplies to families who fled into Kenya after fighting erupted in the Ethiopian border town of Moyale this week and that its response would initially reach 1,000 households.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Kenya Red Cross said it was sending humanitarian supplies to families who fled into Kenya after fighting erupted in the Ethiopian border town of Moyale this week and that its response would initially reach 1,000 households. Hundreds of Ethiopians, mainly women, children and young people, [USN:L8N4681I7 TEXT:"crossed into Kenya"] after the fighting began on Wednesday, the Kenya Red Cross and local government officials have said. Gunfire could still be heard on the Ethiopian side of the border on Thursday, according to local residents. Kenya's Moyale town, which sits opposite an Ethiopian settlement of the same name, remained calm, but police were on high alert after reporting several incidents involving stray bullets. The Kenya Red Cross said it had begun setting up a temporary shelter and distributing tents, blankets, sleeping mats, jerrycans, kitchen sets and fortified porridge flour. "Many have arrived with very few belongings and urgently need shelter, food, water and health care," the organisation said in a statement late on Thursday. A police report seen by Reuters said a stray bullet had lodged in the neck of a local woman in Kenya's Moyale town. She was admitted to a private hospital where the bullet was removed and is now in a stable condition, the report said. Later on Friday, local government officials on the Kenyan side will meet to coordinate humanitarian assistance to displaced households.

item.title: AI trade meets the Fed
item.description: An eye-catching week is in store as rate-setters at the Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and Bank of Japan announce policy decisions, while investors will gauge whether results from Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft can fuel the next leg of the AI rally.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An eye-catching week is in store as rate-setters at the Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and Bank of Japan announce policy decisions, while investors will gauge whether results from Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft can fuel the next leg of the AI rally. Elections in Israel and Brazil, a gathering of China's top leadership and a closely watched British budget add political risk to the agenda. Here's all you need to know about the coming week in financial markets by Lewis Krauskopf in New York, Kevin Buckland in Tokyo, and Dhara Ranasinghe, Marc Jones and William Schomberg in London. 1/ MOVE OVER It's a packed week for central banks. The Fed, Bank of Canada and Reserve Bank of New Zealand meet on Wednesday, the ECB on Thursday, and the [USN:L4N4650G0 TEXT:"BOJ"] a day later. The Fed, ECB and BOJ face no immediate pressure to hike rates after tightening last month. Fed Chair [USN:L6N46606V TEXT:"Kevin Warsh"] will be pressed on his view on the rate outlook. The ECB is sure to face questions about surging [USN:L8N4670MT TEXT:"French borrowing costs"] that risk becoming a flashpoint, while the BOJ may [USN:L4N4650KC TEXT:"raise its inflation forecasts"] in a post-meeting report. Markets expect Canada and [USN:L6N4671E0 TEXT:"New Zealand"] to hike rates to contain inflation, with all policymakers grappling with the extent to which high oil will fuel broader price pressures. 2/ HYPERSCALER HOT SEAT A big week for US [USN:L6N45T17Q TEXT:"corporate earnings"] will be headlined by reports from three of the largest companies at the heart of the huge AI capital investment theme that has driven up equities. Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) and Amazon (AMZN.O) — three of the so-called hyperscalers — will post results at a time investors are becoming wary of the [USN:L6N45Y119 TEXT:"risks"] of the spending on data centres. The week will be critical to determining if the third quarter lived up to high expectations for US profit growth, with about one-third of S&P 500 (.SPX) companies reporting. Other high-profile firms set to report include drugmaker Eli Lilly (LLY.N) , oil majors Exxon (XOM.N) and Chevron (CVX.N) , and industrial equipment giant Caterpillar (CAT.N) . 3/ FISCAL TIGHTROPE British finance minister John Healey will announce his first budget on Wednesday, when he will try to offer some relief from higher [USN:L6N45O0SR TEXT:"energy prices"] to households, but without unsettling the bond market by ramping up [USN:L8N46708T TEXT:"borrowing"]. That means Healey may have to accept a narrowing of his room for manoeuvre to meet his fiscal rules. Analysts polled by Reuters think he can allow his headroom to almost halve to around £15 billion ($20 billion) without spooking the market. [USN:L1N46206Z TEXT:"Banks"] might bear the brunt of tax increases, and the share prices of Britain's biggest lenders have fallen in the run-up to Healey's high-profile debut. Bigger decisions on spending in areas such as defence, public services and welfare are likely to be put off until next year, with Healey hoping the Iran war — and the pressure it is putting on government borrowing costs — may have abated by then. 4/ NETANYAHU'S MOMENT OF TRUTH Israel's [USN:L8N3XX04M TEXT:"election"] on Tuesday is poised to be one of the most consequential in the country's history. Polls have it as a coin toss , with neither Prime Minister [USN:L1N45L0EX TEXT:"Benjamin Netanyahu's"] Likud bloc nor an opposition centred around former military chief Gadi Eisenkot expected to win a majority, raising the prospect of lengthy coalition negotiations. Yet for markets, it also comes after an [USN:L8N46801Y TEXT:"extraordinary rally"] in Israeli assets. Since 2023's October 7 attacks, the Tel Aviv stock market (.TA125) has surged more than 135%, while the shekel is up a world-beating 25%. Analysts are quick to point out the AI boom has been key, given Israel's tech expertise, and will remain so. But investors also see the potential for tensions to be gradually dialled down in the longer term if Eisenkot and his allies can win out. In Brazil, the presidential election will reach its conclusion on Sunday, with markets hoping Flavio Bolsonaro can edge out current President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva after the challenger's surprisingly strong first-round performance sent stocks surging to a [USN:L1N45R06Y TEXT:"record high"]. 5/ PARTY PRIORITIES China's top [USN:L6N4680FF TEXT:"leadership"] gathers in Beijing for the four-day [USN:L1N45D08Z TEXT:"Fifth Plenum"] from Monday, with officials deliberating on "Advancing Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance." That may sound inward-looking, but official Chinese commentary frames the initiative as an effort to strengthen Party discipline and execution in response to a more challenging external environment, including an increasingly tense relationship with the [USN:L8N45K07F TEXT:"United States"] and curbs on China's access to advanced foreign technology. That's not to say Beijing doesn't face [USN:L1N46501H TEXT:"challenges"] at home too, with domestic demand stuck in a prolonged slump that has proved stubbornly resistant to stimulus efforts. ($1 = 0.7470 pounds)

item.title: First Russian diesel from Putin-Trump deal heading for US, data shows
item.description: The first Russian diesel bound for the US following a surprise agreement reached between Moscow and US President Donald Trump is aboard a tanker heading for New York, ship-tracking data showed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The first Russian diesel bound for the US following a surprise agreement reached between Moscow and US President Donald Trump is aboard a tanker heading for New York, ship-tracking data showed on Friday. Trump announced the [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"deal"] this month as part of his efforts to bring down soaring diesel prices ahead of November 3 US mid-term elections. Trump also waived parts of a new US sanctions law against Russia and threatened Europe with a US diesel export ban unless countries released more from their emergency reserves to help ease prices. The Malta-flagged medium-sized tanker Agioi Fanendes was loaded with 40,000 metric tons of ultra-low sulphur diesel in Russia's Baltic port of Primorsk on October 22, according to LSEG shipping data. It is expected to arrive in the United States on November 7. The identity of the buyer and seller were not immediately known. The cargo will be the first imported by the US since former President Joe Biden announced a ban on US imports of Russian oil and petroleum products in 2022. Trump [USN:L1N45V0MW TEXT:"announced on October 9"] that Russia would immediately export 300,000 metric tons, or 2.25 million barrels, to the US and global markets, followed by 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons "immediately thereafter". A Kremlin spokesperson on Friday confirmed a first ship under the deal had departed, but did not specify whether it was bound for the US market or elsewhere. "As far as I'm aware, there have already been reports from the Ministry of Energy that the first tanker has, in fact, set sail for its recipients, its buyers. Further shipments will continue at a steady pace from here on," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on a daily conference call. The deal with the US involved Russia lifting a self-imposed ban on diesel exports. RUSSIA RESUMING GLOBAL EXPORTSSince the EU imposed a full embargo on imports of Russian oil products in February 2023 over the war in Ukraine, Russia has [USN:L6N4320US TEXT:"exported diesel"] mainly to Turkey and Brazil, as well as to African countries. It also [USN:L1N45V0GI TEXT:"supplies"] Central Asia by rail. Shipping data from LSEG and Kpler published this week showed Russian diesel cargoes [USN:L6N4660Q8 TEXT:"resuming voyages"] to their traditional destinations after Moscow lifted its own ban, with at least two tankers signalling trips to Turkey and Brazil. It was unclear where other tankers were destined for, with [USN:L6N4600IE TEXT:"cargoes"] loaded in Primorsk signalling Gibraltar, the Atlantic Coast or Port-Said, LSEG data showed. Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak has said additional US shipments would follow as companies from the two countries work out the necessary contracts. Putin envoy Kirill Dmitriev, who also heads Russia's sovereign wealth fund, said last week that the US Treasury had asked the fund to help sort out tricky [USN:L1N4620KW TEXT:"payment issues"] relating to the agreement. Novak has said that Russia would be able to increase its [USN:S8N45E0D7 TEXT:"diesel exports"] to its usual levels of 3-3.5 million tons per month by year-end.

item.title: Sodexo-CA annuel au-dessus des attentes avec les hausses de prix, le titre grimpe
item.description: Sodexo grimpe en Bourse vendredi après avoir publié un chiffre d'affaires annuel plus important que prévu, le groupe de restauration collective citant notamment des hausses de prix d’environ 2,4%.
item.dc:creator: Rihab Latrache, Ronan Corcoran
item.content:encoded: Sodexo (EXHO.PA) grimpe en Bourse vendredi après avoir publié un chiffre d'affaires annuel plus important que prévu, le groupe de restauration collective citant notamment des hausses de prix d’environ 2,4%. Le chiffre d'affaires de l'exercice s'élève à 23,96 milliards d'euros, en hausse de 2,0% sur un an en organique. Les analystes tablaient en moyenne sur 23,78 milliards et une croissance organique de 1,5%, selon un consensus compilé par l'entreprise. La croissance interne est également soutenue par une hausse des volumes sur les sites existants d'environ 0,6%, "en raison d'une très forte activité de Sodexo Live, notamment sur le deuxième semestre de l'année", a déclaré Thierry Delaporte, directeur général (DG) de Sodexo, durant une conférence téléphonique. À la Bourse de Paris, ces résultats ont été salués et l'action progressait de 6,47% à 60,05 euros vers 11h30 GMT, contre un repli de 0,52% pour l'indice SBF 120 (.SBF120) au même moment. "La marge dans le haut de la fourchette devrait rassurer, tandis que le flux de trésorerie disponible s'est également révélé supérieur aux prévisions", soulignent les analystes de Jefferies. "La publication remplit les critères essentiels et devrait, selon nous, être bien accueillie ce matin", avisent-t-ils dans une note publiée avant l'ouverture des marchés. Le groupe enregistre une croissance interne du chiffre d’affaires de 2,0% et une marge d’exploitation de 3,4%, dans le haut de la fourchette attendue. Le taux de fidélisation clients ressort à 94,4%, avec un développement commercial de 7,7%. "La croissance organique devrait se situer en dessous de la fourchette, puis s’améliorer progressivement au cours de l’année avec l’accélération de l’impact des nouveaux contrats nets", a déclaré le DG à propos de l'exercice 2027, Sodexo confirmant par ailleurs ses perspectives pour l'année prochaine. "Notre orientation claire est d’avoir, pour l’exercice 2027, une marge globalement similaire à celle de l’exercice 2026. Cela signifie environ 3,4%", a ajouté Thierry Delaporte. L'entreprise prévoit pour cette année un déploiement de projets de développement dans les domaines de l’investissement commercial, de la technologie et de l’approvisionnement. Sodexo a précisé ne pas avoir été affecté par la situation politique et sociale en France liée aux [USN:L8N4650AN TEXT:"récentes manifestations"], le pays ne représentant que 12% de ses activités.

item.title: Volvo Cars shares in record plunge on widening losses, job cuts
item.description: Volvo Cars shares fell almost 30% on Friday after the Swedish carmaker posted a far bigger-than-expected third-quarter operating loss and said it would cut a further 2,500 jobs, mostly in its home market Sweden.
item.dc:creator: Marie Mannes
item.content:encoded: Volvo Cars (VOLCARb.ST) shares fell almost 30% on Friday after the Swedish carmaker posted a far bigger-than-expected third-quarter operating loss and said it would cut a further 2,500 jobs, mostly in its home market Sweden. The slump, which takes the shares deeper into record lows, comes as the firm, majority-owned by China's Geely Holding (GEELY.UL), struggles with uneven demand for electric vehicles, mounting tariff pressures and tough market conditions in China. "The third quarter of 2026 was very disappointing and reflects a year that has become far more challenging than originally anticipated. Our ongoing turnaround plan therefore needs a decisive reinforcement," CEO Hakan Samuelsson said. The automaker reported an operating loss of 3.7 billion Swedish crowns ($373 million) in the quarter, versus a profit of 5.8 billion crowns a year earlier. Citi analysts said the consensus forecast was for a loss of 724 million crowns. CEO Samuelsson returned from retirement in 2025 on a two-year contract to turn Volvo around. But despite [USN:L8N3R60KQ TEXT:"harsh"] cost cuts, a regionalisation plan and closer Geely ties, the outlook has only worsened. The carmaker said it needs to trim another 5 billion crowns of costs. The latest measures will affect about 6% of Volvo's workforce, including around 2,000 jobs in Sweden, through the termination of consultant contracts, natural attrition and targeted exit packages, it said. The cuts come in addition to 3,000 job reductions previously announced. Samuelsson told Reuters that the cuts should be completed by mid-2027, although he did not rule out further measures. INCOMING CEO FACES DEEPENING CRISIS Former Skoda boss Klaus Zellmer, who will succeed Samuelsson next year, will need to stem the decline of one of Europe's most well-known car brands. "Zellmer... has an even harder job on his hands now than when he was announced one month ago," Bernstein analysts wrote in a note, saying they struggled to see things improving any time soon. Volvo's [USN:L6N3Y80UT TEXT:"EX60"], an electric version of the best-selling XC60 and central to Volvo's turnaround, has been hit by heavy delays due to issues with battery assembly. Only around 5,000 units of the planned 40,000 for this year have been [USN:S8N40K029 TEXT:"built so far"], the company said. The company [USN:L6N45O0BV TEXT:"scrapped its guidance"] for full-year sales volume and cash flow this month, saying it would prioritise margins over market share in its key market in China rather than join an intensifying price war with domestic rivals, as its third-quarter revenue fell nearly 50%. Volvo's gross margin fell to 14.7% in the third quarter from 20.4% a year earlier, it said. Six of the 13 models Volvo plans to launch by the end of the decade will be designed for China and Samuelsson does not see any improvement in the group's performance there until they start arriving, he said. "We should have maybe realised earlier that we need to be more regional in China, maybe we should have also realised earlier that tariffs would come so we need to localise more in the US," Samuelsson said. "So that's a weakness right now which we are addressing." ($1 = 9.9180 Swedish crowns)

item.title: Morning Bid: Wake up! The long bond's up two points!
item.description: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Wayne Cole.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Wayne Cole. It's not every day you wake up to see the US long bond up 2 full points in price, but that's what happened overnight. Ten-year yields dived 19 basis points in the biggest daily move since early 2023, when Silicon Valley Bank collapsed. Fed funds futures rallied as much as 22 ticks, essentially taking an entire hike off the table for next year, while a December move is no longer fully priced in. Old-fashioned safe harbours were in demand as the yen and Swiss franc climbed, leaving the dollar looking a little less exceptional. The proximate cause this time was the sound of air escaping from the [USN:L6N4681D7 TEXT:"AI bubble"] as investors grappled with the sheer scale of funding needed for all this compute power. Some estimates put it at 1.6 times the cost of laying America's railways. Seems [USN:L6N468125 TEXT:"Meta's"] mention of needing "hundreds of billions of dollars" for capex [USN:L4N4681N3 TEXT:"spooked the horses"], with its shares sliding almost 7%. And not everyone was happy about the dilution from having to establish a whole new class of stock with no voting rights to raise the money. CoreWeave, the data center group that started much of this scare, shed another 10% of its value to hit lows last seen in May 2025, while credit spreads blew out across the entire sector. Treasuries benefited from the resulting scramble for safety, though that "safety" is relative these days. There is also the risk the investment boom in data centres will sputter, stalling a major driver of economic growth. Voter opposition to the energy-hungry sites has also been a notable feature of the midterm campaigns, adding politics to the mix. The surge in Treasuries might bring back memories of the Greenspan put, but it'll be much harder for the Fed to ride to the rescue this time. Brent futures are atop $113 a barrel, and over $100 right out to March, while crude for actual delivery is far higher. Easing monetary policy during an inflationary oil shock is going to be a hard sell. Neither is there any end in sight to the conflict in the Gulf. The press is full of reports of the White House considering fresh attacks on Iran after the midterms. The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier group just departed Japan this week for Exercise Keen Sword 27, after which it will head for the Middle East. Ever since the war started in February, analysts have always assumed it would be done within a month or maybe two. Next week will mark the eighth month of the war, and it's not even clear whether Washington and Tehran are talking to each other. That will ensure inflation is front and centre when the Fed meets next week, relegating Wall Street's woes to a footnote. Key developments that could influence markets on Friday: - October global PMIs for Europe, UK and US. UK and Canada retail sales - Appearance by ECB board member Piero Cipollone (This story has been corrected to fix a typo in paragraph 5.)

item.title: Gold steadies after three-month lows as oil rally fans inflation worries
item.description: Gold prices steadied after hitting a three-month low earlier on Friday but were on track for their steepest weekly loss since June, as rising oil prices fuelled higher-for-longer Federal Reserve rate expectations and pressured the non-yielding precious metal.
item.dc:creator: Vishak Mathew
item.content:encoded: Gold prices steadied after hitting a three-month low earlier on Friday but were on track for their steepest weekly loss since June, as rising oil prices fuelled higher-for-longer Federal Reserve rate expectations and pressured the non-yielding precious metal. Spot gold was at $4,023.95 per ounce by 1210 GMT after earlier dropping to $3,986.50, its lowest since July 20. Bullion has lost 3.5% so far this week, the second consecutive weekly loss. U.S. gold futures for December delivery fell 0.5% to $4,038.40 per ounce. "The rise in oil prices could result in real interest rates remaining higher for longer, which would reduce the relative attractiveness of investing in and holding gold," Hamad Hussain, climate and commodities economist at Capital Economics, said. Brent crude touched a more than five-month high on Friday, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies. Rising oil prices can stoke inflation, prompting investors to scale back Fed rate-cut bets. Last week's US [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"consumer"] and [USN:L1N4610KT TEXT:"producer"] inflation data came in hotter than expected, largely because energy costs keep climbing. That strengthens the case for tighter policy, even though Fed officials are still expected to [USN:L6N46606V TEXT:"hold off"] when they meet on October 27-28. Market expectations of a rate hike at the Fed's October 27–28 meeting are at 9%, while it is 81% for December, according to CME's FedWatch Tool . Investors are also awaiting US Personal Consumption Expenditures data, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, on October 29 for fresh clues on progress toward its 2% target. The [USN:L8N4651KP TEXT:"European Central Bank"] meets on Thursday against a backdrop of upheaval in France and an Iran war that is keeping energy prices above $100, meaning inflation risks remain elevated. Among other metals, spot silver slid 1.3% to $53.84 per ounce, and palladium dropped 0.6% to $1,047.69 per ounce, hitting their lowest since November 2025 and June 2025 respectively. Spot platinum edged down 0.8% to $1,558.18 per ounce, its lowest since July. All three metals were headed for weekly declines.

item.title: Trump says Bombardier to invest $270 million in the US
item.description: President Donald Trump said late on Thursday Canadian jet maker Bombardier was investing $270 million in the United States, days after he dropped threats to ban the company from the country.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump said late on Thursday Canadian jet maker Bombardier (BBDb.TO) was investing $270 million in the United States, days after he [USN:L1N4660P1 TEXT:"dropped threats"] to ban the company from the country. Trump's September [USN:L1N44Z0HG TEXT:"threats against Bombardier"] became a political issue in Kansas, where it employs 1,500 people in Wichita. The threatened ban prompted calls to the White House from Kansas lawmakers, including Republican Senator Roger Marshall, who is facing a tough race in the November 3 elections. Bombardier will recruit for 500 roles across the US and is planning to create an extra 300 jobs through expansion projects, the company said in a statement on Friday. The expansion will include an initial investment of about $270 million for infrastructure growth in the first phase, per the statement. “Based on our constructive conversations with the U.S. administration, we see a bright path forward for our highly skilled aerospace workers as well as a positive environment for Bombardier to continue pursuing direct investments to grow our American footprint,” CEO Eric Martel said. The hiring will be spread across Texas, Kansas, Indiana and Connecticut, the company said. In a Truth Social post late on Thursday, Trump said Bombardier's investment would create thousands of jobs in Kansas, Texas, and Indiana, and credited Marshall along with Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton for the deal. Bombardier, which acquired Learjet and established its US headquarters in Kansas in 1990, has 3,500 jobs in the US, more than 40% of which are in Wichita. At a speech in Wichita on Monday, Trump said he did not plan to hurt Bombardier and would take care of its workers. "... now I find out they have a presence here, and we're not hurting them if they're in Kansas. So we'll take care of those people and the jobs," the president said in that speech. In February, Trump had threatened to decertify Bombardier aircraft over a certification dispute involving rival Gulfstream Aerospace. That threat never materialized because Transport Canada ultimately [USN:L1N3ZK0S8 TEXT:"approved the jets"].

item.title: Ready for a French test?: Five questions for the ECB
item.description: The European Central Bank meets on Thursday against a backdrop of upheaval in France and an Iran war that is keeping energy prices above $100, meaning inflation risks remain elevated.
item.dc:creator: Dhara Ranasinghe, Stefano Rebaudo
item.content:encoded: The European Central Bank meets on Thursday against a backdrop of [USN:L8N4670KY TEXT:"upheaval in France"] and an Iran war that is keeping energy prices above $100, meaning inflation risks remain elevated. "How do you set rates against that backdrop? It's incredibly difficult," David Coombs, head of multi-asset investments at Rathbones Asset Management, said. Here's a look at five key questions for markets ahead of the October meeting. 1/ What will the ECB do? Leave its key interest rate unchanged at 2.5%. A pause is widely anticipated after the ECB raised rates in June and [USN:L1N452054 TEXT:"September"] to counter rising inflation, as the Iran war pushed up energy prices. Economists polled by Reuters [USN:L6N45T0G5 TEXT:"expect a quarter-point rate hike"] in December. "I don't think they've become materially less worried about inflation here," MUFG senior economist Henry Cook said. 2/ What will the ECB say about the rate outlook? It's likely to stick with a data-dependent approach. Caught between high inflation, at [USN:L8N45O0I3 TEXT:"3.8% in September"], and concerns that [USN:L1N45N082 TEXT:"rising government bond yields"] could hurt growth, policymakers have recently argued for what ECB President Christine Lagarde called a "[USN:L8N45K12P TEXT:"measured response"]." "There will be a definite flag to the tightening in financial conditions and how it should slow growth and hence curb inflationary pressures," said Barclays' head of euro rates strategy Rohan Khanna. "But also, plenty of uncertainty around the conflict and the outlook for energy prices." 3/ How worried is the ECB about an energy-driven inflation rise? Comments from officials such as ECB chief economist [USN:S8N3YE046 TEXT:"Philip Lane suggest"] the ECB is not overly worried, for now, about high energy costs leading to other prices and wages rising. A muted increase in core inflation, which excludes food and fuel prices, to [USN:L8N45O0I3 TEXT:"2.5% last month from 2.4%,"] suggests that high energy costs have yet to generate the sort of second-round impacts that could set off a hard-to-break inflation spiral. Still, with oil up almost 80% this year and headline inflation above its 2% target, the ECB will likely stress vigilance. "If the war in Iran escalates, or if we see further pressure on energy prices, the risk is still more rate hikes in 2027," said Bas van Geffen, senior macro strategist at Rabobank, adding he did not have any penciled in for next year. Markets price in at least two hikes by mid-2027. 4/ What about the French bond selloff? Well, the ECB is watching. French 10-year borrowing costs just hit [USN:L8N4670MT TEXT:"24-year highs above 5%"] and a weakened government is grappling with violent protests that could undermine efforts to improve fragile finances. Also, the premium investors demand to hold 10-year French bonds over safer Germany is at 170 bps, up from 92 bps when the ECB met last month. But don't expect the ECB to act soon with measures such as the [USN:L1N45N0CH TEXT:"Transmission Protection Instrument"] that allows it to buy bonds from any member state experiencing an "unwarranted, disorderly" tightening of its financing conditions. France should [USN:L1N46002V TEXT:"solve its own debt problems"] through fiscal consolidation, says Lagarde. The ECB could hold back on rate hikes if it thinks a crisis in France could hurt economic growth materially, Berenberg chief economist Holger Schmieding said. "If there are serious contagion effects from a hypothetical French crisis to other countries where the fiscal policy is much more sustainable, the ECB would probably use its TPI to shield these other countries, not France," he said. 5/ Who will replace Lagarde? The ECB chief, who could be appointed as the [USN:L6N4610XU TEXT:"next World Economic Forum chair"] as early as November, will likely be pressed on succession. The former central bank governors of the Netherlands and Spain, [USN:FWN45G19M TEXT:"Klaas Knot"] and Pablo Hernandez de Cos, are seen as frontrunners. Lagarde's exit would open a second vacancy on the ECB's six-member Executive Board after [USN:L6N45V0R7 TEXT:"Isabel Schnabel's recent resignation"]. Chief economist Lane is meanwhile due to step down in May. Lagarde's term is scheduled to end next October. Leaving early allows time for a new ECB chief to be picked before France's spring presidential election. A snap Spanish election could also impact the [USN:L8N46305T TEXT:"politics around ECB succession"], analysts said.

item.title: Oil spill off UAE coast prompts beach closures, cleanup effort
item.description: The United Arab Emirates said efforts were under way on Friday to contain oil leaking from a tanker vessel offshore that prompted authorities to close beaches and warn fishermen to avoid the area.
item.dc:creator: Maha Dahan, Sarah Safty
item.content:encoded: The United Arab Emirates said efforts were under way on Friday to contain oil leaking from a tanker vessel offshore that prompted authorities to close beaches and warn fishermen to avoid the area. Since the start of the US-Israeli war with Iran , attacks on commercial vessels in Gulf shipping lanes have driven up security risks for maritime traffic and heightened fears over the conflict's environmental fallout. The UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment said in a statement that containment operations had been launched and an environmental assessment was being carried out. All beaches and coastal areas around the city of Umm Al Quwain had been temporarily closed until technical teams completed their assessments and determined the necessary safety and marine protection measures, it said. The ministry also urged fishermen and other sea users to avoid affected areas and follow official instructions. ANALYST IDENTIFIES LEAKING TANKER AS THE GEM NO.2 UAE authorities have not named the tanker involved in the incident or said what caused the spill. And the environment ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. However, Martin Kelly, CEO of Orbital Risk Intelligence, told Reuters that the spill was coming from a tanker called the Gem No.2. Shipping sources said on October 9 that the Gem No.2 was [USN:L1N45V0GU TEXT:"struck"] by an unidentified projectile 13 nautical miles west of Al Jazeera in the UAE, causing a fire that was later extinguished. While no group claimed responsibility, maritime security sources told Reuters at the time that the incident occurred outside the Strait of Hormuz and pointed to a widening of risks for commercial shipping. Earlier that week, a tanker was also struck off the coast of Qatar inside the Gulf. SPILL PUTTING COASTAL INFRASTRUCTURE AT RISK Maritime intelligence firm Windward first identified the spill on Tuesday, writing in a post on X that a VLCC-sized vessel was leaking oil about 25 km (16 miles) off Umm Al Quwain. Prevailing currents, it said at the time, could carry the slick southwest toward the UAE coastline. "Windward's drift model shows it reaching Sharjah's and Ajman's desalination intakes and ports by (October 22–23) if the leak isn't stopped," it wrote on X. The UAE relies on desalination plants for most of its drinking water, and much of the economy — including ports and industrial facilities — is also located on the coast, making any contamination along its shoreline particularly sensitive. Residents in some areas had posted on social media about strange odours. The ministry, however, said that odours reported in Sharjah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain posed no health risks. The spill follows a [USN:L8N4490KK TEXT:"separate"] tanker-related environmental incident in August, when oil from a tanker that ran aground off Oman began reaching the mainland coast.

item.title: Data centres fail as AI pick-and-shovel trade
item.description: NextDC shares fell 42% after community backlash delayed power upgrades at one site. Investors are wising up to the trade-offs of massive debt-financed spending, slow-moving utilities, chip shortages and impatient hyperscaler clients like OpenAI with ironclad get-out clauses.
item.dc:creator: Antony Currie
item.content:encoded: So much for a safe bet on the AI revolution. The smart advice for investing in potential bubbles is to find the modern equivalent of the picks and shovels of the US gold rush in the 1800s. For today's artificial intelligence trade, data centre providers were supposed to be one of them: no matter whether hyperscalers like OpenAI and Anthropic or any of the other developers of software succeed or fail, the demand for places to host the hardware needed is too strong to shatter. But the stock price crashes at Australia's NextDC (NXT.AX) and its US neocloud rival CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , and the [USN:L6N45V00W TEXT:"aborted $5.5 billion IPO"] of Firmus Technologies, confirm that investors are realising it's not that simple. Start with the non-financial problems. Data centre developers want to build as fast as possible to meet their hyperscaler clients' voracious demand for compute and inference capacity. Trouble is, that can lead to high expectations, poor planning and dismal community relations, even for players like NextDC, whose shares fell 42% on Wednesday, that have been in operation for decades. Semiconductor shortages continue, for example. And utilities need more than a few months to get water and electricity hooked up - one water provider told Breakingviews conversations ought to start up to three years before developers buy the land. Nscale in the UK [USN:L6N4650TB TEXT:"lost a contract"] with Microsoft (MSFT.O) after being told power would not be available until 2030. NextDC similarly misread local opposition to its M3 site in Melbourne right across the street from a residential neighbourhood: the resulting delays to installing up to 22-metre-high concrete poles to carry 66,000-volt cables forced CEO Craig Scroggie to slash its EBITDA forecast by a third, cease projects with no contracts and consider selling undeveloped sites. Such issues can then cascade. Constructing data centres requires lots of investment. That's mostly done with debt, usually raised only once a contract has been signed. While that sounds smart, it leaves the borrower at the mercy of iron-clad get-out clauses. One is the availability clause: if water or power connections are delayed by a stipulated timeframe, if a natural disaster strikes or if chips are either unavailable or subpar, then the hyperscaler client can walk. There's also a more general delay clause, which usually stipulates the customer can cancel the entire contract if completion of the data centre is more than 12 months late. It's bad news for traditional data centre builders and neoclouds alike. They could be left with the unenviable mix of part-finished projects, unused land, underwhelming or no earnings and heaps of debt. Hardly a picks-and-shovels trade. Follow Antony Currie on Bluesky and LinkedIn . Shares in NextDC closed down 42% on October 21 after the Australian data centre builder and operator cut its underlying EBITDA forecast for the financial year to the end of June by more than a third. The company now expects EBITDA of A$245 million to A$265 million ($172 million to $186 million) for the period. CEO Craig Scroggie also said he is putting on hold all projects not already backed by customer contracts, has started a "detailed review" of the company's capital expenditure programme and is open to selling development sites that "are not required in the near term". The move came after Jemena Electricity Networks informed NextDC that it has suspended some of the work to increase power supply to its M3 data centre in Melbourne following "community and stakeholder opposition". Last month local residents used their vehicles and other methods to prevent Jemena from installing concrete electricity poles of up to 22-metres in height that are needed to carry the 66,000-volt power lines the data centre will require. Scroggie also noted that the company had some A$8.7 billion of liquidity at the end of September. Meanwhile, on October 20, after local opposition Amazon abandoned plans to build four data centres on a site it had bought from George Washington University in Virginia in the US. The company also agreed to donate $5 million to the county's housing trust fund. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: Brent crude hits more than five-month high on concern over Middle East escalation
item.description: Oil prices rose on Friday, with Brent crude touching a more than five-month high, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie Kelly
item.content:encoded: Oil prices rose on Friday, with Brent crude touching a more than five-month high, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East. Brent crude futures gained $1.40, or 1.2%, to $114.57 a barrel by 1138 GMT, having earlier reached $115 for the highest level since May 4. US West Texas Intermediate crude gained $1.48, or 1.5%, to $100.95. The Brent benchmark is on track for a third consecutive weekly gain, of 4.2%, while WTI is poised to finish 0.5% down on the week. Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) on Thursday [USN:L1N46809Q TEXT:"ordered the evacuation"] of its headquarters in Dhahran on the Gulf near Bahrain, Reuters reported, as fighting intensified between the world's largest crude exporter and Yemen-based Houthis. "The market remains concerned about a potential escalation, which, in a worst-case scenario, could trigger renewed supply disruptions," said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo, adding that volatile oil flows and elevated freight rates have left the market undersupplied. Clashes between the Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition that backs Yemen's internationally recognised government have raged since the Iran-aligned Houthis pushed towards Bab el-Mandeb, a shipping chokepoint at the mouth of the Red Sea. "The key factors to monitor now are the extent of actual disruption and the time needed to restore operations, as these will ultimately determine how much of a supply risk premium the market is willing to pay," said XS.com analyst Linh Tran. "If attacks persist and delay deliveries, elevated prices will have a firmer foundation." An oil spill from a tanker [USN:L1N469029 TEXT:"was detected"] off the coast of Umm Al Quwain, prompting containment operations and environmental assessments, the United Arab Emirates Ministry of Climate Change and Environment said on Friday. The ministry did not say what caused the spill and authorities have not identified the tanker involved. In Libya, an oil pipeline valve from the Hamada and Tahara oilfields to Zawiya port has been shut, leading to a reduction in production at both fields, the head of the National Oil Corporation told Reuters on Thursday. Meanwhile, the first Russian diesel [USN:L1N4690EB TEXT:"bound for the US"] since a surprise agreement between Moscow and US President Donald Trump is aboard a tanker heading for New York, ship-tracking data showed on Friday. Trump announced the [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"deal"] this month as part of his efforts to bring down soaring diesel prices ahead of US midterm elections next month.

item.title: US corporate profit boom faces its ‘Minsky moment’
item.description: Earnings for the S&P 500 Index rose 26% in the past year. Tech giants and chipmakers at the heart of the AI boom make up more than half the surge. Depreciation delays and investments in unlisted firms inflate bottom lines. As the economist Hyman Minsky wrote, it cannot last.
item.dc:creator: Edward Chancellor
item.content:encoded: The artificial intelligence generated by large language models is breathtaking. Equally wonderous is the financial alchemy that accompanies multi-trillion-dollar investments in AI infrastructure. Capital spending is instantaneously transformed into profits, even as the economic viability of the AI buildout remains questionable. The United States is in the throes of a great profit boom.
